Martin ruled on 2026-11-18: add a failure timeout for a leased job whose agent goes silent. The Control Plane fails the job (not re-queue) once its agent sends no heartbeat or worker event within JobRouting:SilentLeaseTimeout (default 2 minutes); its dependents fail with it and a re-run resumes.

Found and fixed during the #171 live runs (2026-11-18, 'you find it you fix it'), each test-first: (1) the TFS agent's generic ClassificationTreeCapture replaced TfsClassificationTreeCapture after the guard removal, so every TFS Export failed to start (TryAdd); (2) a job that threw was never reported, leaving it leased for 16 h (AgentWorkerBase reports it failed); (3) the Aspire default 10 s resilience timeout cut the agent's 30 s lease long-poll (RemoveAllResilienceHandlers, EXTEXP0001 suppressed on that call); (4) TFS export wrote link types with ToString(), and non-directional ends as Related-Forward (reference names now); (5) the Azure DevOps target sent relative related-link URLs (full URL now); (6) Selection.Query was never applied to export on either connector and the pre-pass skipped itself in Migrate mode for want of an endpoint (query now bounds the selection pass, which falls back to the job's source endpoint); (7) the TFS agent registered no IWorkItemFetchService or IAttachmentBinarySource (per-job adapters added). CliRunnerTimeoutTests now uses a 1.5 s timeout because the simulated export finishes in about 3 s once (3) is fixed.
